version.changelog: v2.0.1: category/tags now required, add prerequisites & quick config section, sync with GitHub

llm.summary: This skill is meant to manage a Typecho blog, but the package includes a live-looking blog URL and API token that could let installed agents publish, update, or delete content on that configured site.

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose coherently matches Typecho blog create/list/get/update/delete operations, but the shipped config.json contains a concrete domain and bearer token rather than placeholders, giving immediate write-capable access to a specific remote blog.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill uses broad triggers such as writing notes, archiving, knowledge base, and my blog, while create and update flows can directly modify remote content; only deletion has an explicit second confirmation step.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact includes persistent configuration with an apparent real API token, so installation may carry credentials and target configuration not supplied by the installing user.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Network API access and stored credentials are expected for a blog-management integration, but direct publishing as the default status and bundled credentials make the authority higher than a generic documentation skill.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill explicitly instructs persistent storage of the blog domain and token and says configuration is reused without repeated asking; combined with the included token, this creates durable remote mutation authority.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Review carefully before installing. Replace or remove the bundled config.json credentials, ensure the token belongs only to your own Typecho site, prefer draft or confirmation-gated publishing, and require explicit confirmation for create/update/delete operations.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] unexpected: The broad trigger concern is supported by the artifact: common phrases can activate a skill that creates, updates, and deletes posts. This is not malicious by itself, but it compounds the risk from direct publishing and bundled credentials.
[VirusTotal] expected: VirusTotal telemetry is clean and does not add negative evidence.
[staticScan] expected: Static scan reported no suspicious patterns, but static cleanliness does not resolve the credential and scoping concerns visible in the artifacts.
